speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what caused HDB to make erroneous payments of CPF housing grants to ineligible applicants as highlighted in the Annual Report of the Auditor-General’s Office for FY2020/2021; and (b) in what manner will HDB be improving its controls over the processing and assessment of CPF housing grants.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB assesses each application by manually verifying, amongst other things, the declared incomes against the documents submitted by the applicants and their occupiers, such as pay slips, employers’ letters, commission statements, CPF contribution histories and Notices of Income Tax Assessment.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For ownership of private property, HDB will verify documents such as the Notice of Transfer, Transfer Instrument, and Sale and Purchase Agreement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The verification process is often complex, especially when flat buyers and their occupiers have multiple sources of income and/or property ownership, both local and overseas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These applications involved a total of 47,808 applicants and occupiers.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Of the 13 applicants, HDB has since verified that one applicant had in fact been correctly assessed for the grant disbursement.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This omission was not detected in the verification checks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: HDB is also implementing process improvements and automating eligibility check processes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will allow HDB to more efficiently and accurately assess the eligibility of the very many grant applicants, even if they fail to declare any material information to HDB.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And thank you to Minister Indranee and Minister Edwin Tong for replying my Parliamentary Questions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have supplementary questions for Question Nos 4 and 7.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: For Question No 4 to Minister Indranee, this year's AGO report was unusual in that there were a number of Ministries and Statutory Boards observed to have documents altered, backdated, artificially created or falsified.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Hence, my Parliamentary Question was to inquire into the number of investigations and individuals involved, to get a better extent of the size of these infractions and the number of people involved.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In view of information that the Minister has just shared and her reply that efforts will be stepped up to resolve some of these issues, can the Minister share what is the nature of these efforts, do they include more frequent internal audits, for example, or intensive contract management and procurement-related training programmes for the relevant personnel?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I understand that PA's internal investigation went beyond the test checks that were done for the contract variations with regard to the two development projects.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm that PA also will be making an announcement on the results of these findings when the investigations are complete, in view of the statement that was released on 22 July 2021.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second supplementary question for Minister Tong is: is there a process or procedure in place to bar companies including managing agents for all Government-related tenders that are found to have been flagged out by AGO for significant irregularities, for example, like the managing agent identified at paragraph 56 of the AGO report which found irregularities in more than 90% of payments that were test checked?

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He had asked what efforts are being taken to address this because there were a number of infractions across various Ministries and agencies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I think we can break it down to two responses that would be appropriate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As you can see from the lapses, one is a process problem.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For the process problem, the key is to be able to pick this up as quickly and as efficiently as possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And the key to that is lies in having more automated processes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: That way, hopefully, you minimise human error and you are able to flag up the inconsistencies or the red flags as and when they occur.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The second and the more important one is really the people part.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Partly, it is building capability, but the other part is impressing upon public officers the importance of doing this well and carrying out these functions well, so that in fact, they internalise it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In addition, Heads of Agencies will prioritise and intensify our internal audits to look out for any such wrongdoing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: And when such issues are detected, we will deal with them decisively.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, our public officers, do recognise that public accountability remains a top priority for the Government and they are committed to addressing the lapses identified and resolving the problem at the root and this includes strengthening organisational, capabilities, systems and processes to prevent future recurrence.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, in relation to the second question on whether we will take into account findings, all of such findings will be appropriately addressed.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: There is a framework to consider, to assess when tenderers come in to make bids.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth and Second Minister for Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All of these, including the antecedent behaviour of a particular individual or contractor, will be taken into account when assessing and judging on these bids.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: My question is for the Second Minister for Finance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Would the Minister require all the remedial and recovery action that is to be reported to AGO be presented to Parliament when completed, to give public closure to these lapses and violations?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Essentially, what happens is that we have the Public Accounts Committee which is a committee of Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Public Accounts Committee can enquire from the Ministry what the updates are.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Ministry will reply and the reply is effectively to a committee of Parliament, so it is as if it is to Parliament.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And the Public Accounts Committee will then issue a public report.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is Ms Foo Mee Har.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The significant observations arising from AGO's audit of the two development projects under the People's Association (PA) are disturbing.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth to clarify the following.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: One, whether the lapses uncovered in contract management are systemic across the development projects.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It is surprising to hear that PA actually manages 788 projects at any one time.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Second, whether the root causes of irregularities have been identified and isolated, and if new projects that are now ongoing need to be suspended, pending the consultants' study of the issues that have been uncovered.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The lapses, as far as we can tell, were not systemic.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But at the same time, as I have mentioned earlier, we have already immediately implemented some changes to improve the system and oversight governance functions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We will also subject our oversight and governance of such matters to a professional external review, as I have mentioned.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And I have mentioned that an external consultant has been appointed, being given a broad mandate to look at these governance systems and oversight functions.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The lessons that we have learnt, the immediate steps that we have taken on board will, of course, be shared with any new projects that will come on board.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And thereafter, after we have done a full review, we will strengthen and continue to strengthen these processes.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have mentioned, PA oversees a wide range of development and redevelopment projects for more than 780 such facilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But what is important is to be able to detect it, to pick it up and then act firmly against it.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, it is important to have a strong audit system, both internal and also external.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And on top of that, regular AGO audits which go deeper into specific matters.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We take each case of lapse very seriously.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And in this case, as Members know, once PA became aware of these findings, an internal investigation was carried out immediately.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This led to staff being suspended and a Police report was filed; all of these even before AGO disclosed its findings.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As I have mentioned earlier, we also are investigating transactions beyond the scope of AGO's sampling.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In many ways, Sir, we are tougher on ourselves when lapses are discovered.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We must continue to do so and build a strong culture of zero tolerance, particularly when it comes to questions of integrity and probity of transactions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister for National Development.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The first is, besides clawing back the grants that were wrongly paid, HDB has stated that it would also take enforcement action against those who have suppressed material information.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like the Minister to confirm whether HDB, by saying this, accepts that there could be some cases where the applicant did not act deliberately but there could have been some genuine misunderstanding about the eligibility criteria or the information that needed to be provided.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: My second question: HDB has stated that AGO has asked HDB to report back on the remaining 1,055 cases which were picked up by data analysis which could have involved wrongful payment of grants.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Could the Minister tell the House how long does HDB expect to take to finish these investigations and confirm that the Ministry will make the findings public as well?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of the instances of suppression of material information may have been deliberate; some of it may have been a misunderstanding.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will have to look at it case by case.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have two supplementary questions for Minister Edwin Tong.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: PA has identified and appointed the external consultant.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can Minister share with us the identity of this external consultant?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And if it has started work, it will be helpful to share with us the findings progressively.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And I would like to know what kind of timeline we are looking at in sharing the findings with us.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: As to sharing the findings progressively, we will certainly do so internally as and when lessons learnt or options become available to improve processes.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: My supplementary question is for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Our Tampines Hub (OTH) is very popular with residents.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: So, I would like to know if the operations, events and services at OTH have been affected by observations highlighted in the AGO report.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Yes, the staff obviously have been affected in that they have been cooperating with AGO.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, they have had to put aside time to deal with that and also with the internal investigations that we continued with, over and above what AGO has done to ensure that we look at all the remaining contracts that OTH had entered into.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: At the same time, it is also important to keep the functions and facilities of OTH running, making sure that residents' and businesses' interests are not compromised, ensuring that the tenants that remain at OTH will also be looked after.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, there is a wide range of other responsibilities that the staff are looking into.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And it is important to ensure that there is enough resourcing and staffing to see to this.
